prompt: Customer support filed BUG_REPORT.md — they can't find users via the search endpoint when the casing of the email doesn't exactly match what was stored. The repo at /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/evals/rca/fixture has the failing test (tests/test_search.py) and the relevant code under app/. Do a proper root-cause analysis: I want to understand why this happened (not just patch the search), whether the same problem exists elsewhere in the codebase, and what would prevent the whole class of bug. Write the report to OUTPUT_DIR/report.md.
assertions: Report file exists at outputs/report.md and is non-empty (>1000 chars).
Report cites or runs the failing test (mentions tests/test_search.py or test_search_finds_user_signed_up_with_mixed_case).
Report contains a 5-whys chain as a numbered list with at least 4 distinct Why questions.
Each Why link in the chain cites concrete evidence — at least 4 file:line-style citations (e.g., app/db.py:NN, app/signup.py:NN) appear in the chain.
Report explicitly labels symptom / proximate cause / root cause (all three words appear with their corresponding statements).
Root cause identified is the missing email normalization at write time (signup stores the raw email), NOT merely 'search uses == comparison'.
Sibling sweep identifies at least two of: app/password_reset.py, app/invite.py, app/signup.py (the other call sites of db.find_by_email).
Report presents both a symptom fix and a root-cause fix as distinct options with a recommendation.
Counterfactual section confirms that under the recommended fix, the failing test would now pass (or names which 5-whys link the fix breaks).
Prevention proposal includes at least one of: a regression test, a guardrail (type/schema/lint), or a doc update — and aims at the class, not just this instance.
Load-bearing assumptions are enumerated as a numbered list with validation results.
